thread:
emma (support): FYI AcmeCorp reported 502s right after our cert rollout to their Private VPC. They see TLS handshake failures from their clients. Paste of their error: "certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate"

noah (sre): Can you paste the customer repro steps and any server logs? Also did our rotator show a successful deploy for that tenant?

emma (support): They said they didn't change anything client-side. Steps they ran: first request successful, then after ~5m a flurry of 502s. They did an app retry and some requests succeeded. Shared logs: 
```
2026-03-10T12:03:21Z gateway ERROR TLS handshake failed: alert handshake failure (unknown_ca)
2026-03-10T12:03:21Z http ERROR client_conn: certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate
```
They also ran openssl and attached output (trimmed):
```
openssl s_client -connect private.acme.example.com:443 -servername private.acme.example.com -showcerts
depth=0 CN = private.acme.example.com
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
```

emma (support): I queried dig from two of their DNS resolvers and got different answers (split-horizon?)
```
dig @10.1.2.3 +short private.acme.example.com -> 10.0.4.22
dig @10.1.2.4 +short private.acme.example.com -> 10.0.8.19
```

sophia (eng): Hmm. Two different backends, but the certs served should be identical. Could be that one LB (10.0.4.22) still had old chain, or our HAProxy instance cached an incomplete chain after reload. Any rotator event for tenant?

rotator-bot: Rotation completed for tenant acme-tenant at 2026-03-10T12:00:58Z. New cert chain uploaded: chain-v2026-03-10-12.

noah (sre): Also saw note in support ticket: their egress NAT IP changed around the same time (cloud provider rehoming). If their firewall allowlist only contained the old egress IP then callbacks to OCSP/CRL or cert validation flows could fail from their infra, causing partial failures. Could also cause sticky sessions to break if SNAT changed midstream.

emma (support): They confirmed they have strict allowlist for our health-probes and ocsp endpoints. Suggested repro: 1) run curl from inside their VPC to our endpoint 2) run dig against both resolvers 3) check openssl verify chain and tcpdump during handshake.

sophia (eng): Quick checks for them to run:
```
# check chain served by each backend
openssl s_client -connect 10.0.4.22:443 -servername private.acme.example.com -showcerts
openssl s_client -connect 10.0.8.19:443 -servername private.acme.example.com -showcerts
# DNS glue check
dig +short @10.1.2.3 private.acme.example.com
dig +short @10.1.2.4 private.acme.example.com
# see egress ip used
curl https://ifconfig.me -s
```

noah (sre): Proposed immediate mitigation for customer: add the new egress IP to their allowlist (or a /28 if provider rotates), and ask them to flush local DNS caches (pods, apps) so they stop talking to stale backend. Also instruct them to check any firewall stateful timeout — NAT ephemeral port reuse plus egress IP change can make backend see mismatched connections.

emma (support): I sent these steps. They ran the commands and returned outputs: one backend (10.0.4.22) served a certificate chain missing the intermediate (chain trimmed), the other served full chain. Their egress IP was different from the one in their allowlist.

sophia (eng): That explains the verify error: clients hitting the trimmed-chain backend will fail to build the chain. Two root causes aligned: our rotation gave a new chain (ok), but one LB worker did not pick up the full bundle on reload -> incomplete chain; and their egress IP change blocked ocsp/remote fetching for some clients.

noah (sre): Action plan:
- Support to confirm customer added new egress IP into allowlist and validated OCSP/CRL egress. (emma)
- SRE to check LB instances for partial bundle and force reload on the affected nodes. (noah)
- Eng to add a rotator post-check that queries multiple LB nodes for chain completeness post-rollout. (sophia)
- If customer still has issues, consider short rollback to prior chain while we remediate.

emma (support): Customer updated allowlist and confirmed callbacks to ocsp.example.com are allowed. We forced a reload on their LB via control-plane (permitted) and the svc now returns full chain consistently. They report no further 502s after 6m. :thumbsup:

sophia (eng): We'll add a post-rotation verification job (quick openssl/s_client to a few nodes) and a rotator signal if any node returns an incomplete chain. Filing ENG ticket to track.

noah (sre): I'll also add a note to run a NAT egress reconciliation check during private deploys to detect provider-induced IP changes.

emma (support): Closing loop with customer and documenting repro steps in the ticket. Thanks team.
